title: Uniform topological moduli space for a finite-diagonal Deligne--Mumford stack
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $\mathcal X$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack over $k$ as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Suppose its relative diagonal $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$ is finite: every scheme base change is a scheme finite over the base [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. There exist an algebraic space $M/k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and a morphism $c:\mathcal X\to M$ with the following two properties. First, $c$ is uniform categorical: for every flat morphism $M'\to M$ of algebraic spaces over $k$, every morphism $\mathcal X\times_M M'\to Z$ to an algebraic space $Z/k$ factors uniquely through the projection $\mathcal X\times_M M'\to M'$. This includes the identity base change, so $c$ is initial among morphisms to algebraic spaces over $k$. Flatness of algebraic-space morphisms is tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Second, $c$ is a universal homeomorphism: for every Deligne--Mumford stack $\mathcal Z/k$ and morphism $\mathcal Z\to M$, the map $|\mathcal X\times_M\mathcal Z|\to|\mathcal Z|$ is a homeomorphism. Here points and topology are those of [lem-sfb-stack-topology-open-substacks], also applied to algebraic spaces as stacks with trivial automorphisms. In particular $|c|:|\mathcal X|\to|M|$ is a homeomorphism. Schemes are [def-pc-scheme].

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori), specialized to Deligne--Mumford stacks with finite diagonal; Tag 0DUG (definition-categorical-quotient). The finite-inertia hypothesis follows because the inertia projection is the base change of the relative diagonal along itself. Universal homeomorphism means stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 0CI7 (definition-universal-homeomorphism).

proof.text: The inertia $I_{\mathcal X}$ is the 2-fibre product $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X}\mathcal X$, both maps being the relative diagonal. Indeed an object consists of two objects and two isomorphisms between them; identifying the two objects by the first isomorphism leaves an object and an automorphism. Its projection to the second factor is therefore the base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}$. For every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, its further pullback is exactly the scheme base change of that diagonal along $T\to\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$. Thus the hypothesis of finite diagonal gives finite inertia, in precisely the scheme-test convention required below.

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori), finite-inertia hypothesis; the fibre-product computation is elementary.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-keel-mori-finite-inertia-quotient] over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$. It gives an algebraic space $M/k$ and a categorical map $c:\mathcal X\to M$ which is a universal homeomorphism. In particular the second property in the item already holds, since every Deligne--Mumford test stack is an algebraic-stack test allowed by that node. Taking the identity test $M\to M$ gives $|\mathcal X|\cong|M|$. It remains to prove that this same $c$ has the asserted factorization property after flat base change. Categorical choices cause no ambiguity: if $d:\mathcal X\to P$ is another one, their two factorization properties give maps $u:P\to M$ and $v:M\to P$ with $ud=c$ and $vc=d$. Then $(uv)c=c$ and $(vu)d=d$, so categorical uniqueness gives $uv=1_M$ and $vu=1_P$. The equalities $ud=c$ and $vc=d$ identify the quotient maps. On a 2-fibre-product test object, apply $u$ or $v$ to its algebraic-space component and to its structural identification; the identities $uv=1_M$ and $vu=1_P$ make these operations inverse. This gives the corresponding cartesian diagrams for the chosen categorical map.

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori), existence and topological assertions; reuse the existing finite-inertia categorical-quotient node.

proof.text: Choose the jointly surjective separated representable etale maps $g_i:\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal X$ and the affine finite locally free groupoid presentations $\mathcal X_i\simeq[U_i/R_i]$ from [lem-sfb-finite-inertia-etale-affine-charts]. Each $\mathcal X_i$ is Deligne--Mumford: pull back an etale scheme atlas of $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal X_i$, refine the resulting etale algebraic spaces by their etale scheme charts [def-trf-algebraic-space], and compose. These charts cover $\mathcal X_i$ and are etale by base-change and composition stability in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]; representability of its diagonal is part of being an algebraic stack. Each chart has finite inertia, since its inertia projection is the pullback of that of $\mathcal X$ by the asserted inertia isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-groupoid-moduli] to the specified presentation: $c_i:\mathcal X_i\to M_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ is uniform categorical, hence categorical at the identity base change. The $g_i$ preserve inertia, so [lem-sfb-keel-mori-stabilizer-preserving-etale] gives separated etale maps $r_i:M_i\to M$ and equivalences $\mathcal X_i\simeq\mathcal X\times_M M_i$. The $r_i$ cover $M$: for $m\in|M|$, choose $x$ above it using $|c|$ surjective and then $x_i$ above $x$ using joint surjectivity; $c_i(x_i)$ maps to $m$.

source.place: Tags 0DUE, 0DUP, 0DUR, 0DUV; cartesian local models and their joint surjectivity.

proof.text: Let $b:N\to M$ be any flat algebraic-space morphism over $k$ and put $\mathcal Y=\mathcal X\times_M N$. Set $N_i=N\times_M M_i$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], the $N_i$ are algebraic spaces and $N_i\to N$ form an etale covering. All maps here are maps of algebraic spaces, hence representable by algebraic spaces. Over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, the flat map $N_i\to M_i$ is the base change of $b$; apply the arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Associating the 2-fibre products identifies $\mathcal Y\times_N N_i$ with $\mathcal X_i\times_{M_i}N_i$. On a scheme test $T$, both sides consist of triples $(x,n,m_i)$ with $c(x)=b(n)=r_i(m_i)$; arrows are isomorphisms of $x$ fixing $n,m_i$. Keeping this triple and its arrows gives inverse functors, compatible with pullback in $T$ and with projection to $\mathcal Y$. For an algebraic space $Z/k$ and a map $\theta:\mathcal Y\to Z$, restrict $\theta$ to these identified stacks. The uniform property of $c_i$ gives unique maps $\psi_i:N_i\to Z$ whose composites with these projections equal the restrictions of $\theta$.

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori), last paragraph, local factorizations after arbitrary flat base change; Tag 0DUR supplies their universal property.

proof.text: On $N_{ij}=N_i\times_N N_j$, compare the two restrictions of $\psi_i,\psi_j$. The projection $N_{ij}\to N_i$ is etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; it is flat, and $N_{ij}\to M_i$ is flat, by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] applied over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ to these representable maps of algebraic spaces: etale implies smooth implies flat, and $N_{ij}\to M_i$ is the composite of the flat maps $N_{ij}\to N_i$ and $N_i\to M_i$. Write $p_i:N_{ij}\to N_i$, $p_j:N_{ij}\to N_j$ and $e:\mathcal Y\times_N N_{ij}\to N_{ij}$. Pulling back the two equalities constructed in step 4 gives $(\psi_i p_i)e=\theta\operatorname{pr}_{\mathcal Y}=(\psi_j p_j)e$: both maps to $\mathcal Y$ forget exactly the two chart coordinates. Thus the two candidate maps have identical composites with $e$. This stack is $\mathcal X_i\times_{M_i}N_{ij}$ by the cartesian identification already obtained. The injective part of the uniform bijection in [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-groupoid-moduli], for the flat map $N_{ij}\to M_i$, forces $\psi_i|_{N_{ij}}=\psi_j|_{N_{ij}}$. This writes out the agreement on overlaps without assuming a separate quotient theorem for the overlap stack.

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori), last paragraph: the omitted agreement-on-overlaps argument.

proof.text: Glue the compatible $\psi_i$ to $\psi:N\to Z$ using that algebraic spaces are sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Explicitly, for a scheme $T\to N$, refine the etale cover $T\times_N N_i$ by etale scheme charts. The maps from these charts to $Z$ agree on overlaps by the previous step, so the sheaf axiom gives a unique element of $Z(T)$. For $T^\prime\to T$, the pulled-back section and the section constructed on $T^\prime$ have the same restrictions on the pulled-back cover, hence are equal by sheaf uniqueness. Thus these sections define a natural transformation $N\to Z$. For any scheme object $T\to\mathcal Y$, the maps $T\to N\xrightarrow{\psi}Z$ and $T\to\mathcal Y\xrightarrow{\theta}Z$ agree on the induced etale cover, so they agree by the same sheaf axiom. Thus $\psi$ factors $\theta$. If $\phi$ is another factorization, its restriction to each $N_i$ equals $\psi_i$ by the categorical uniqueness established in step 4. Testing on scheme charts and using sheaf uniqueness gives $\phi=\psi$. Since $b, Z,\theta$ were arbitrary, this proves uniformity, including the identity base change.

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori), last paragraph: sheaf gluing, factorization, and uniqueness, written on scheme tests.
